The challenge and competition. Other methods of entertainment are not as mentally engaging as video games. Better yet, none of them have you determine the outcome.

Books, television and movies are great, but they progress and end the same way. Competitive video games have a different progression every time.

It depends really. When I was younger, I used to love the competition and being the best. Basically loved twitch gaming like UT99, Quake 3, U2k4, etc.

Then I really got into the strategy aspect and played Diablo 2 and Starcraft non stop. Followed by Warcraft 3, and several other games. I really enjoyed the depth to these games and the crazy shit you could do. At one point in time I literally spent all of my free time watching online replays of Starcraft and Warcraft games, looking at the pros, trying to learn new strategies and predict what strategies my enemies are using.

Then I got into RPG's and really enjoy the story and how you can basically get lost in games. Baldur's Gate series, The Witcher series, etc are really great at that and I really enjoyed the story and environment in these games.

Nowadays I basically only really play games for fun, but the fun varies drastically. For example I've wasted a ton of time on a few games in the past couple of years, but I generally don't play much any more. Dwarf Fortress I can play for 12+ hours non stop. Same with Borderlands (I just fucking love it for some reason). Terreria, Skyrim and this weird city builder called Banished. Each one I like for different reasons, and play differently. Sometimes I won't touch a game for months, then I spend like 80 hours on Borderlands 2 in two weeks, it's really weird.

I think what I really like the most about games is the reality. If you can create a good, believable, and attractive reality, then everything else becomes easier since you already have the players undivided attention. Of course this requires a mix of sound, art, creativity and imagination. Not exactly easy to pull off.

In a book/movie/whatever, you often get to watch the protagonist go from relatively powerless to very powerful. In a video game you get to experience it first hand. Would you rather see something cool happen, or be the thing yourself? This is the power of video games. No other medium can make you the protagonist in that way.
